## Ticket proposals
- **A deliverable glob containing [email] matches nothing, so no agent can write the account page** — suggested P1; declined by Spud: Real and confirmed, but the fix is in Spud's own repository rather than BadTakes, so it is recorded there as SPD-086 (P1) with Snowden's evidence and the two candidate fixes. Nothing is dropped: BAD-054 PR 2 plans its deliverable as admin/src/app/accounts/?email?/**, which is verified to match..
  Why: The edit hook reads a deliverable as a glob, so the literal directory name [email] becomes a character class matching one of e/m/a/i/l and no real path under admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/ ever matches. Every agent on BAD-054 is therefore read-only on the exact files it owns, including PR 2, which has to rewrite UserTab. A reviewer told to fix a defect in place cannot.
  Evidence: Refused with: 'Law 5: admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/page.tsx is not among BADS-054/Snowden's deliverables (admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/**)' for both a cp and a shell redirection, while my planned deliverable is exactly admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/**. I worked around it by doing the before-render and all fault injections in rsync copies under my scratchpad, so the worktree stayed byte-clean. A fix is either escaping glob metacharacters in a deliverable that names a Next.js dynamic segment, or matching deliverables as literal path prefixes when the glob has no wildcard outside the trailing /**.
- **The spike's render-diff recipe is guaranteed to fail, and cannot see the dropped key it claims to catch** — suggested P1; created as [[BAD-074]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: Section 8 step 5 of docs/spikes/bad-036/admin-account-page.md is PR 2's primary proof. As written it produces a false failure on every run and a false pass on one of the three drifts section 10 names, so PR 2 needs both fixed before it starts or its reviewer will spend the run rediscovering them.
  Evidence: Two build-fingerprinted values survive the recipe's perl, which strips only script blocks: the /_next/static/ asset URLs in the head, and the Server Action ids in each control's hidden inputs. Running the before and after phases as two builds gave 532 diff lines from those alone. I proved they are build artifacts, not render differences, with a control run: identical source built at a second path produced exactly the same two action-id differences and nothing else, and all twenty ids in .next/server/server-reference-manifest.json differ between the two builds, including actions on pages the split never touches. Normalising the asset URLs, the action id and the ACTION-KEY value makes pre-split and post-split byte-identical across 76 documents. Separately, section 10 says the render diff catches a dropped key. It cannot: React never writes a key into HTML, and the RSC payload that does carry one lives inside the script tags the recipe strips. I removed the key prop from the usage rail's Link and rebuilt: zero difference in any of the 76 documents, while the same build's wrong-side conditional, licenses.length greater than 1 changed to greater than 0, showed up immediately on eight user tabs. In PR 1 verify-moves catches a dropped key because the declaration moves whole; in PR 2 it will not, so a key becomes a drift that only reading the diff can catch.

## Result
Verdict: BAD-054 PR 1 is a pure move and preserves the page. I changed nothing; the worktree is exactly as I found it (git status clean, untracked included) and commit 40c7135 stands as written. Ran the spike's section 8 steps 1-5 from my own baseline, page.old.tsx taken from origin/main (a0baf97, which is also 40c7135's parent) and both scripts transcribed into my scratchpad. Step 1: npm run verify with the fake-CI environment, exit 0; eslint's only warning is the pre-existing one in components/Rail.tsx. Step 2: the three admin tests, 11 pass, 0 skip. Step 3: export diff empty, default with the same props type plus dynamic. Step 4: OK, 20 statements, every one moved exactly once, and no COMMENT LOST or COMMENT ADDED at all. Placement matches the plan's accounting file by file, 5+2+1+2+3+2+2+2+1. Two checks beyond the recipe: the orchestrator region of the old file, lines 28-53 and 84-192, diffs byte-identical against the new page.tsx; and the multiset of all 1117 non-import, non-blank source lines is byte-identical across the split, which pins every comment and every JSX comment in place, not merely present. Section 10: no new file carries a client directive; the only async in the tree is flagsOrNull in _lib, the planned data guard called from AccountPage's inSeries, and the five components contain no async, await or Promise; USAGE_RAIL, LOGS and the stubs are in plain modules; the controls come in by the components alias. requireAdmin() is the first statement and notFound() is at line 75 before any JSX, and neither symbol appears in any sub-component. The inSeries literal the pool test reads is still in page.tsx. The URL contract holds, checked by fetching tab=profile, a bare tab=usage, no query and a bogus tab and metric. Step 5 ran: the stack was already up at migration 0043 and npm run seed rewrote only its own 10 rows, so BAD-047's worktree was undisturbed. 76 documents per phase, 9 accounts by 8 views plus the 4 URL-contract cases. Because my deliverable glob is unusable (proposal 104) I could not swap the page in place, so the pre-split phase was built from an rsync copy of admin under my scratchpad with node_modules and the repo-root paths symlinked. Result: identical everywhere except two Server Action ids, which a control run proved is a build artifact of the second path and not a render difference. Normalised, before and after are byte-identical across all 76. Fault injections, all in scratch copies: idStub's slice length changed by one token, verify-moves FAIL exit 1; the usage rail's key prop removed, verify-moves FAIL but the render diff saw nothing at all; licenses.length greater-than-1 changed to greater-than-0, verify-moves FAIL and the render diff flagged exactly the 8 single-licence user tabs and left gil alone. All reverted, injected tree diffs clean against the worktree. On BAD-070: Dakota's countdown extension is sufficient here and I would keep it. Both of countdown's numeric forms are covered, the seeded cooldowns sit about 21 hours out so neither can cross the hour boundary or reach 'now' during a session, and it is applied to both phases, so it can only hide a difference in a clock-derived string, which is what it is for. Its only untreated outputs are the empty string and 'now', both stable; normalising a bare 'now' would be too broad to be worth it unless a seed row is ever given an expired cooldown. Not re-filed: the five vestigial banner comments, confirmed present in flags-or-null, LogsTab, UsageTab and twice in UserTab, which is BAD-071. Nothing left open on PR 1 itself; the two things I could not prove are the hand check of section 6 (I never opened a control dialog, only confirmed the controls' serialised props are identical) and that the route table still lists the page as dynamic, which I take from the export contract rather than from build output I truncated.
